landscape.title: The zeta landscape
landscape.noWebgl: WebGL is not available on this device.
landscape.legend: Color = direction (argument) of ζ(s), brightness = size (darker is closer to 0; the pole at s = 1 is white). Around a zero every color appears once. White circles mark computed zeros — all on the dashed line Re = ½. The 'trivial zeros' hide at −2, −4 on the real axis.

offline.title: A world where the hypothesis fails
offline.on: All zeros at β = ½: the error wiggles evenly inside the √x band.
offline.off: One zero off the line: its wave grows like x^β and drags the error out of the band. The real primes (black) don't.

spacing.title: Zero spacing histogram
spacing.small: Share of spacings < ¼: zeta {{zeta}}%, GUE {{gue}}%, uranium nucleus {{nuclear}}%, random {{poisson}}%. Zeros and nuclear levels both repel.
spacing.nuclearNote: Measured: {{n}} neutron-resonance level spacings of uranium-238 (evaluated nuclear data JEFF-3.3, 0–10 keV, spin ½). Nuclei are time-reversal symmetric, so they follow GOE: repulsion slightly weaker than zeta zeros (GUE). Near 0 the curve grows like s (GOE) vs s² (GUE).
spacing.gueNote: GUE is the random-matrix model physicists built for heavy nuclei; here we simulate it directly.

ai.title: 2026: two records
ai.gaugeTitle: ① Share of zeros proven to lie on the critical line (lower bound)
ai.gaugeNote: Claude (Anthropic, Aug 2026): 41.6% → 67.2%. The Riemann hypothesis claims even more than filling this bar to 100%.
ai.stripTitle: ② Width of the strip that traps the zeros
ai.stripNote: The narrower the strip, the more we can say about primes. But no strip, however narrow, is a single line. One line remains out of reach.
